name: MD-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+30 partisan lean strongly favors Democrats
Incumbent Jamie Raskin running with a $7.9 million cash advantage
Republican challenger raised under $17,000 with no outside support
Prediction markets price Democratic win at 97%
model.rationale: The fundamentals point overwhelmingly to Raskin: a D+30 district, a well-funded incumbent, and a challenger with negligible resources. Markets and the structural baseline agree this is not competitive.
model.watch: Only an unforeseen scandal or incumbent retirement-level shock could move this race, and no such evidence exists.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jamie Raskin seeks another term in this heavily Democratic Maryland district, where the partisan lean runs roughly thirty points in Democrats' favor. He enters the general election with a large financial edge, holding nearly $7.9 million on hand after raising over $7.4 million, while Republican Cheryl Riley has raised about $16,600 total. A Green Party candidate is also on the ballot but lacks any reported fundraising.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Democrats roughly a 97 percent chance of holding the seat. With no competitive spending, no polling showing vulnerability, and a district this lopsided, the outcome is effectively predetermined barring extraordinary events.
